correctness.rationale: For -1<gamma<0 the cube symmetric-difference formula gives exactly the required weak scaling. At gamma=-1 jumps diverge logarithmically, while the compactly supported Cantor staircase has matching Holder and Minkowski exponents that make the endpoint level-set integral finite. Exact kernel integrations lift the one-dimensional endpoint witness to every dimension without removing its singular derivative.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The 2024 BSVY paper and arXiv:2609.19029v1 were checked for the exceptional-range inclusions; the latter proves strict Hardy-Sobolev embeddings into W^{1,1}(gamma) and BV(gamma) and uses the natural W-to-BV inclusion, but the inspected statements and proof do not assert its strictness or give the endpoint Cantor witness. Exact and synonymous literature searches and the current SCOPE archive produced no matching theorem. The open-range witness is elementary and the closest source is very recent, so unindexed or informal prior observation remains possible.

value.rationale: The result completes the strict ordering H^{1,1} subsetneq W^{1,1}(gamma) subsetneq BV(gamma) across the whole exceptional interval [-1,0). The endpoint also identifies a singularity transition: jumps are admitted for -1<gamma<0, fail logarithmically at gamma=-1, but a singular-continuous Cantor derivative remains admissible.
